query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Tailored post-solidification annealing that induces nanoscale interfacial nanoprecipitation (e.g., Hf-rich particles) along the lamellar colony boundaries will improve both room-temperature tensile strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys by reinforcing the weak internal interfaces against microcrack initiation while providing additional precipitation strengthening.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies featuring numerous internal boundaries that serve as sites for microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
generation.intervention: A tailored post-solidification annealing treatment designed to induce nanoscale nanoprecipitates along the lamellar boundaries.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature tensile deformation following the annealing process, with optimized annealing temperature and duration to prevent undesirable grain coarsening or phase changes.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale interfacial nanoprecipitates generated along the lamellar colony boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The nanoprecipitates enhance local cohesion at the otherwise weak interfaces, thereby mitigating microcrack initiation and propagation. Additionally, they contribute to precipitation strengthening of the alloy matrix, leading to improved overall strength without sacrificing ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unmodified (as-cast) lamellar-colony baseline, the annealed alloy is predicted to exhibit higher yield and ultimate tensile strengths along with increased tensile ductility at room temperature, due to a reduction in microcrack formation along the interfaces.
generation.baseline: The unmodified eutectic HEA with dual-phase lamellar colonies and numerous internal boundaries that are prone to initiating microcracks under room-temperature tensile loading.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects depend on the annealing parameters (temperature, time) which must be carefully controlled to ensure optimal nanoprecipitate size and distribution. Excessively long or high-temperature treatments that lead to grain coarsening or unwanted phase transformations could negate the improvements.
generation.uncertainty: The critical nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction required to achieve the optimal balance between strength and ductility remain uncertain and may require further optimization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare specimens of the eutectic HEA with identical composition. Apply the tailored post-solidification annealing to a set of samples while keeping a control group in the as-cast state. Use varying annealing temperatures and durations to generate a range of nanoprecipitate sizes and distributions. Perform room-temperature tensile tests and microstructural analysis on both treated and untreated samples.
measurements: TEM characterization to quantify nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction along the lamellar boundaries
Room-temperature tensile tests to determine yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility
Fractography to document the initiation and propagation of microcracks relative to interfacial regions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the annealed samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and ductility compared to the as-cast baseline, or if no correlation is observed between nanoprecipitate formation at the lamellar interfaces and a reduction in microcrack initiation during tensile testing.

cited_evidence.text: In this paper, we designed and prepared All7Cr10Fe36−xNi36Mo1Hfx dual-phase high-entropy alloys (x = 0, 0.03, 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.8 in at%) with FCC and B2 phases. Firstly, the same thermal and mechanical treatment was conducted on the All7Cr10Fe36−xNi36Mo1Hfx cast alloy to eliminate segregation and solidification defects in the cast alloy. Then, a systematic study was conducted on the effect of Hf content on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the All7Cr10Fe36−xNi36Mo1Hfx alloy. The addition of Hf can simultaneously improve the high-temperature strength and ductility of the matrix alloy in the temperature range from 600 °C to 900 °C, especially at 700 °C. The strengthening and toughening mechanisms at 700 °C in the All7Cr10Fe35.5Ni36Mo1Hf0.5 alloys were analyzed by comparing the differences in fracture behavior and microstructure between the Al17Cr10Fe36Ni36Mo1 and Al17Cr10Fe35.5Ni36Mo1Hf0.5 alloys.

The room-temperature strength of Al0.3CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys (HEAs) is relatively low owing to its intrinsic fcc structure. In the present study, the as-cast HEAs were subjected to cold rolling and subsequent annealing treatment (800, 900, and 1000 °C) to adjust the microstructures and tensile properties. This treatment process resulted in the partial recrystallization, full recrystallization, and grain coarsening with increasing the annealing temperature. It was found that the large and spherical B2 precipitates were generated in the recrystallized grain boundaries of three annealing states, while the small and elongated B2 precipitates were aligned along the deformation twins in the non-recrystallized region of the 800 °C-annealing state. The former B2 precipitates assisted in refining the recrystallized grains to quasi ultra-fine grain and fine grain regimes (with the grain sizes of ~0.9, ~2.2, and ~7.2 μm). The tensile results indicated that the decreased annealing temperature induced the gradual strengthening of this alloy but also maintained the ductility at the high levels. decision.trend: Early EHEA studies demonstrated that casting to form dual-phase (e.g., fcc/B2) lamellar colonies could yield high strength and ductility at room temperature. Subsequent work refined these cast microstructures by using thermo‐mechanical processing (including cold, cryo, and warm rolling) to obtain ultrafine or dual heterogeneous structures that further enhanced strength (often via precipitation or grain refinement) while aiming to arrest microcrack propagation. Although these processing routes provided incremental strength–ductility improvements, they did not directly address the intrinsic weakness of the numerous internal (lamellar) boundaries where microcracking initiates.
decision.unsolved: The fundamental issue of microcrack initiation at the internal boundaries of the lamellar colonies remains unresolved—even when strategies improve strength, the interfaces continue to serve as crack nucleation sites, limiting room-temperature tensile ductility.
decision.lever: Tailored post-solidification annealing designed to induce nanoscale interfacial nanoprecipitation along the lamellar boundaries
decision.why: This approach follows the observed trend of using processing modifications to generate heterogeneous microstructures, but it more directly targets the weak interfaces that trigger microcracking. The induced nanoprecipitates at the interfaces are expected to enhance local cohesion and arrest crack initiation, thus simultaneously improving strength (via precipitation strengthening) and ductility (by toughening the boundaries). This intervention is testable by comparing the microstructure, internal flaw density, and room-temperature mechanical performance with the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, and its outcome would falsify the hypothesis if the nanoprecipitation does not reduce microcrack formation or if mechanical properties deteriorate.
